issues_fixed.resolution: Separated the ideal sampling and reconstruction route in Sections 4.1-4.3 from the practical analog anti-alias route in Section 4.8.1 and zero-order-hold/reconstruction route in Section 4.8.4.
Added Orfanidis Chapter 1 Sections 1.3-1.6 to the formal source list, covering the theorem, signed aliases, Poisson replication, sinc interpolation, zero-order hold, compensation, and postfiltering.

Qualified reconstruction by known uniform T_s, a declared bandlimited Fourier/L2 class, the complete exact ideal sample sequence, a declared reconstruction band, and strict replica separation; equality now requires a zero-endpoint or equivalent explicit convention and retains the phase-dependent Nyquist counterexample.
Froze sinc(u)=sin(pi u)/(pi u), the dimensionless argument (t-nT_s)/T_s, unit sample-time kernel height, and the distinct gain-T_s ideal reconstruction filter that cancels the 1/T_s replica scale.
Specified f_s=4 kHz and f=1.3, 5.3, and 10.7 kHz, the half-open interval [-f_s/2,f_s/2), the exact-tie choice -f_s/2, and the signed-direction/real-cosine phase mapping.

Confined interference to 2.6-3.4 kHz with negligible energy elsewhere, froze at most 0.1 dB passband ripple through 1.6 kHz and at least 60 dB attenuation from 2.6 kHz upward, and made the 8 kHz rate-only conclusion conditional on that support bound.

Froze the arbitrary |f|<=4.0 kHz lowpass class, exact four-tone display mixture, separate 12-case tone/phase bank, ideal sample-only reconstruction including equality projection, common unaligned M=512 time grid, relative L2 metric, display floor, and strict pass rule; explicitly excluded sparse-tone recovery framing.

Froze the 6.00-10.00 kHz candidate range on a 0.25 kHz grid and the 0.50 kHz Nyquist-clearance gate, yielding 9.00 kHz as the unique lowest grid pass while naming 8 kHz only as an unsafe continuous-rate infimum.
